game: Arizona State Sun Devils@Texas Tech Red Raiders

guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers lean slightly more toward Texas Tech than the market, largely because Arizona State may have trouble sustaining drives. We rate Texas Tech among the nation’s best at preventing scoring opportunities and defending the run, while Arizona State has struggled in both areas. The Sun Devils converted only 29.6 percent of their third downs through four games, and their rushing average had fallen from 193.62 yards per game in 2025 to 149.0. We are not reacting to one recent result; the broader efficiency profile creates the concern.

The other side of the matchup also favors Texas Tech. Our numbers show a significant advantage for its offense in creating scoring opportunities against Arizona State’s defense. The Sun Devils entered the season with four new starters in the secondary and allowed 15 plays of at least 20 yards through four games. That gives Texas Tech a plausible route to separation, but the market is already accounting for most of it.

For us, that last point determines the decision. We see football reasons to favor Texas Tech more than the market does, but the disagreement is too narrow to create enough value at the available price. The matchup supports our lean, not a wager.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Arizona State’s passing game against Texas Tech’s scoring-opportunity prevention. If the Sun Devils cannot run efficiently, Cutter Boley will carry more of the burden after throwing for 1,040 yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions through four games. Reed Harris gives him a legitimate playmaker after producing 499 receiving yards and five touchdowns over that span.

The useful question is whether Arizona State can turn completions into drive-changing gains before Texas Tech ends possessions. The Sun Devils averaged 8.1 yards after the catch per reception through four games, so there is some volatility here. If Texas Tech contains that element, our projected game script becomes much easier to reach.

recent_game.fact: Arizona State fell to 2-2 overall and 1-1 in the Big 12 after a 55-19 home loss to Baylor on Oct. 3.
Arizona State gained 409 total yards against Baylor, including 310 passing yards, but allowed 564 total yards, 320 passing yards and 244 rushing yards.
Cutter Boley completed 25 of 43 passes for 304 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Baylor.
Reed Harris caught seven passes for 125 yards against Baylor, while Omarion Miller had five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown.
Linebacker Owen Long recorded a season-high 14 tackles against Baylor; Martell Hughes had eight tackles and two tackles for loss, and C.J. Fite had four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss and one sack.

opponent_notes.fact: Texas Tech was ranked No. 11 and stood 5-0 overall and 2-0 in the Big 12 through Oct. 3; the Red Raiders had a bye on Oct. 10 before hosting Arizona State on Oct. 17.
Arizona State's Oct. 17 game against Texas Tech is scheduled for Lubbock, Texas.

quarterback.fact: Kentucky transfer Cutter Boley was named Arizona State's starting quarterback before the 2026 opener.
Through four games, Boley completed 78 of 127 passes for 1,040 yards, 10 touchdowns and three interceptions while adding 45 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown.
Boley threw at least one touchdown pass in each of Arizona State's first four games.
Arizona State averaged 272.8 passing yards per game through Oct. 3, ranking fifth in the Big 12.

Colorado transfer Omarion Miller entered the season after leading Colorado in 2025 with 45 receptions, 808 receiving yards and eight touchdowns.

defensive_personnel.fact: Defensive lineman C.J. Fite had started 31 consecutive games and recorded 83 tackles, 14.5 tackles for loss and five sacks in 42 career games.
Linebacker Owen Long led Arizona State with 39 tackles through four games, 10 more than any teammate, and averaged 9.75 tackles per game.
Martell Hughes ranked second on the team with 29 tackles and led Arizona State with 5.5 tackles for loss through four games.
Michigan State transfer Jalen Thompson had 15 quarterback pressures through four games, tied for fifth in the Big 12, with a 20.2 percent pass-rush win rate.
Arizona State had four new starters in the secondary after losing cornerbacks Keith Abney and Javan Robinson, who had started 26 consecutive games together before the 2025 Sun Bowl.
